boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Fort Sumter II record (August 17-December 31, 1863) in Operations Against the Defenses of Charleston [April-September 1863]. The frozen interval covers the first bombardment (August 17-23) and the second (from late October); the siege of Wagner (SC007) and the September 8 boat attack (SC009) are separate records. Campaign-wide marches, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force text names the Morris Island batteries (US) and the Fort Sumter garrison (CS); the live field reads zero. Gillmore lists the breaching batteries by name and caliber; Jones says twelve batteries mounted twenty-eight heavy rifles and twelve mortars, forty pieces, and that the garrison was Rhett's First South Carolina Artillery until it was replaced by the Charleston Battalion on September 4.
claims.rationale: Gun counts and unit identifications only; no garrison strength. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live result Indecisive. Gillmore reported Sumter reduced to a mere infantry outpost on August 24 and the southeast face a ruin after the second bombardment, which ended aggressive operations for the season; Jones says the fort's garrison held out and the campaign virtually ended with the second bombardment.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads zero. Jones gives the first day's Sumter loss as one man killed and three lieutenants and ten men wounded, and says that during the Morris Island operations the fire that demolished Sumter killed only 3 and wounded 49; he also reports Captain Rodgers killed in the Catskill on August 17.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Jones's 3 and 49 cover a period that ends on September 7, not the frozen interval.

open_questions: The Fort Sumter bombardment reports (Rhett's, Elliott's and the Union battery reports), Turner's supplementary report and Beauregard's general report remain deferred; no Confederate return for the frozen interval was inspected.

NPS/CWSAC (NPS battle page and frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Quincy A. Gillmore's report dated February 28, 1864 (Official Records I, XXVIII part 1, No. 2) is one family of interested Union accounts. Samuel Jones's The Siege of Charleston (1911) is a posthumous Confederate general's history that quotes Gillmore's, Seymour's, Strong's, Ripley's, Taliaferro's and Beauregard's reports and is not independent of them. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
